label: Minimax_H3_fl2va
notes: workflow.json is the source of truth from here on (Harry continues from it, not from his original export). Claude's edits to the original:
1. Load Image node 114 retitled nuke_load_image -> nuke_first_frame.
2. Added Load Image node 129 titled nuke_last_frame, wired to last_frame on nuke_MiniMaxH3_i2v.
3. Int nodes 105_124 and 105_125 retitled nuke_steps and nuke_lightning_steps.
4. Added PrimitiveFloat node 130 titled nuke_fps (24), wired to fps on nuke_create_video and to values.b on the Math Expression (105_107), whose expression now uses 'a * b' where it had 'a * 24'.

knobs.name: duration
knobs.label: duration (s)
knobs.tooltip: Length in seconds. The frame count is duration x fps, rounded up to the model's grid (5, 22, 39, 56 ... frames). The model was trained on about 5 to 15 s at 24 fps.

knobs.name: fps
knobs.tooltip: Frame rate of the clip. Linked to the project's fps; remove the expression to set it by hand. The model was trained at 24 fps: at other rates motion plays slightly faster or slower, and the audio track no longer matches the picture's length.

knobs.name: steps
knobs.tooltip: Sampling steps when the lightning LoRA is off.

knobs.name: lightning
knobs.label: lightning LoRA
knobs.tooltip: Use the turbo LoRA with its own, much lower, step count. Much faster, lower quality.

knobs.name: lightning_steps
knobs.label: lightning steps
knobs.tooltip: Sampling steps when the lightning LoRA is on. The LoRA is made for 8.

knobs.name: codec
knobs.tooltip: How ComfyUI encodes the video that Nuke reads back. All are intra-frame, so scrubbing in Nuke is fast. H.265 is left out because Nuke can't read it.
